matching_criterion: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (vaginal yeast infection), uncomplicated. Any wording that names vulvovaginal candidiasis / vaginal yeast infection counts as correct; bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis or pelvic inflammatory disease as the final diagnosis does not.

management_reference.management: Treat with an azole antifungal (oral or vaginal).
management_reference.source_quote: The mainstay of treatment for most cases of uncomplicated VVC is azole antifungals

management_reference.management: Oral and vaginal azoles are equally effective in clinical treatment of VVC.
management_reference.source_quote: does not indicate a difference in the effectiveness of clinical treatment of VVC between oral and vaginal azole drugs

management_reference.management: With topical azoles the course is about 3 days and symptoms should resolve within 2 to 3 days after.
management_reference.source_quote: Treatment with topical azoles usually lasts 3 days, and symptoms should resolve within 2–3 days after

management_reference.management: Confirm the diagnosis with vaginal pH and wet-mount microscopy.
management_reference.source_quote: Recommendations and guidelines require the collection of a vaginal swab for testing, pH assessment, odor test, and wet-mount microscopy

management_scoring_note: Only items with a verified source quote are scored; general good practice that the article does not state is not scored.
